title: Chern relation for a filtration by line quotients
statement:
Use the finite coefficients, twists and ordinary Chern classes of [def-pur-conventions], [def-pur-chern-classes]. Let $S$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $F$ a rank-$r$ locally free module with a filtration by vector subbundles $0=F_0\subset\cdots\subset F_r=F$ with invertible quotients $Q_j$ as in [def-pur-complete-flag-bundle]. Put $x_j=c_{1,A}(Q_j)$ [lem-pur-kummer-additivity]. Then, with $c_0=1$ and the empty product convention,
$$\sum_{i=0}^r c_i(F)u^i=\prod_{j=1}^r(1+x_ju)\quad\text{in }\bigoplus_{i\geq0}H^{2i}(S,A(i))[u].$$
In particular $c_r(F)=\prod_jx_j$. This holds for nonsplit filtrations and for singular $S$.

source.place: Tag 0FI5, proposition-chern-class (multiplicativity), and Tag 0FI7, lemma-splitting-principle; application to finite-coefficient cohomology for blueprint Step 4 (L4)

proof.text: Write $R_X=\bigoplus_{i\geq0}H^{2i}(X,A(i))$ with cup multiplication. The full-support instance of lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality makes this a commutative graded ring: $(-1)^{(2i)(2j)}=1$. For a rank-$d>0$ bundle $V$ put $P_V(v)=\sum_{i=0}^d(-1)^ic_i(V)v^{d-i}$. The current def-pur-chern-classes defines $c_i(V)=(-1)^{i+1}a_{d-i}$, where $(a_j)=\Phi_{V,d}^{-1}(h_V^d)$; hence $P_V(h_V)=0$. This is the unique monic relation of degree $d$ whose coefficient of $v^{d-i}$ comes from $H^{2i}(X,A(i))$: subtract two such relations, and injectivity of that same degree-$2d$, twist-$d$ map $\Phi_{V,d}$ makes every coefficient zero. The map is precisely the cohomology instance of thm-pur-projective-bundle-formula written in the definition. We prove the stated formula by induction on the length $r$, for all bases and all filtrations in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0FI5, proposition-chern-class, defining relation (equation-chern-classes) and coefficient uniqueness

proof.text: If $r=0$, the left polynomial is $c_0(F)=1$ and the empty product is $1$. If $r=1$, $F=Q_1$; by lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry the projection $\mathbf P(F)\to S$ is an isomorphism and its $\mathcal O(1)$ corresponds to $F$. Thus the defining degree-one relation is $h-c_1(F)=0$, giving $c_1(F)=c_{1,A}(Q_1)$, with the same Kummer convention. These establish both base cases without forming $\mathbf P(0)$.

source.place: Tag 0FI5, proposition-chern-class, invertible-bundle paragraph; rank-zero convention of the item

proof.text: Assume $r\geq2$ and the induction claim for length $r-1$. Set $L=F_1=Q_1$ and $G=F/L$. Use the subbundle terminology of def-pur-complete-flag-bundle: the ambient quotient is locally free. We apply it to the filtration assumed in this item's statement, not just to the universal filtration of that definition. Locally trivialize each $Q_j$ and lift its basis section along $F_j\twoheadrightarrow Q_j$; after refining the open neighbourhood these lifts exist by sheaf surjectivity. Inductively the lifts give an adapted frame of $F$, whose first vector spans $L$. Quotienting deletes that vector, so $G$ is locally free of rank $r-1$ and its filtration $F_j/L$ has line quotients $Q_2,\ldots,Q_r$ and locally free ambient quotients. The induction claim therefore applies over the same possibly singular $S$. No global splitting is used.

source.place: Tag 0FI5, proposition-chern-class, line-subbundle argument, applied recursively to the quotient filtration

proof.text: Let $p:P=\mathbf P_S(F)\to S$ and $P'=\mathbf P_S(G)$. Use the canonical quotient $p^*F\to\mathcal O_P(1)$ and its frame formula from def-pur-complete-flag-bundle. The quotient $F\twoheadrightarrow G$ gives $i:P'\hookrightarrow P$, the locus where this tautological quotient kills $p^*L$. In a local splitting $F=L\oplus G$ and frame $e_0,e_1,\ldots,e_{r-1}$, this is the equation $X_0=0$. On the chart $X_j\ne0$, $j>0$, it is $X_0/X_j=0$, a polynomial variable over the arbitrary affine base ring, hence a nonzerodivisor. On the chart $j=0$ its locus is empty and its equation is $1$. These descriptions glue since they express the vanishing of the globally defined map $p^*L\to\mathcal O_P(1)$. Therefore $P'$ is an effective Cartier divisor. The restricted tautological line is $\mathcal O_{P'}(1)$: both are the quotient of $G$ with chart generator $e_j$ and transition $X_j/X_l$.

source.place: Tag 0FI5, proposition-chern-class, proof: the regular section cutting out P(F) inside P(E) for a line kernel

proof.text: The preceding regular section is a section of $M=\mathcal O_P(1)\otimes p^*L^\vee$. Its evaluation identifies $M^\vee$ with the Cartier ideal: in the displayed charts it sends a basis to the nonzerodivisor $X_0/X_j$. Dualizing gives $\mathcal O_P(P')=M$ by def-pc-divisor-line-bundle. Put $h=c_{1,A}(\mathcal O_P(1))$ and $x=c_{1,A}(L)$. Additivity and pullback in lem-pur-kummer-additivity give $c_{1,A}(M)=h-p^*x$: first $c_{1,A}(\mathcal O)=0$ by additivity, then $c_{1,A}(L^\vee)=-c_{1,A}(L)$. P and P' are separated finite type over k, as the locally projective bundles of the cited geometry statement over S, so their cohomology and Cartier maps lie in the stated finite-coefficient domains.

source.place: Tag 0FI5, proposition-chern-class, line-subbundle paragraph: divisor line and additive first Chern class

proof.text: Form $a=P_G(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(-1)^ip^*c_i(G)h^{r-1-i}\in H^{2r-2}(P,A(r-1))$. Its restriction to $P'$ is zero: $i^*h=c_{1,A}(\mathcal O_{P'}(1))$ by the tautological identification and Kummer pullback, and the resulting expression is exactly the defining relation for $G$. By lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map, the Cartier divisor $P'$ has a supported class $\beta$ with support-forgetting image $c_{1,A}(M)=h-p^*x$; the supported-Hom identification of lem-pur-supported-hom reads that morphism as $\beta\in H^2_{P'}(P,A(1))$. Apply lem-pur-closed-supported-cup-vanishing with $X=P$, $Z=P'$, $\alpha=a$, $b=2$, $s=1$, $a$-degree $2r-2$ and $t=r-1$. It gives $a(h-p^*x)=0$. Commutativity in Step 1 therefore gives $(h-p^*x)P_G(h)=0$. This verifies the divisor-annihilation input, rather than assuming the five axioms of Stacks Tag 0FI4 for this cohomology theory.

source.place: Tag 0FI5, proposition-chern-class, proof of line-subbundle multiplicativity; axiom (5) of Tag 0FI4 verified using supported cup vanishing

proof.text:
Expand the monic polynomial $(v-x)P_G(v)$. Its coefficient of $v^{r-i}$ is $(-1)^i(c_i(G)+x c_{i-1}(G))$, with $c_{-1}(G)=0$ and $c_r(G)=0$. Step 6 says its evaluation at $h$ is zero, and every coefficient has the required degree and twist. The uniqueness from Step 1 implies, for $0\leq i\leq r$,
$$c_i(F)=c_i(G)+x c_{i-1}(G).$$
Consequently $\sum_{i=0}^rc_i(F)u^i=(1+xu)\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}c_i(G)u^i$. This coefficient comparison proves the line-subbundle formula here; it is not delegated to a new Whitney or filtered-bundle lemma.

source.place: Tag 0FI5, proposition-chern-class, end of line-subbundle paragraph; corrected coefficient calculation

proof.text: The induction hypothesis of Step 3 gives $\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}c_i(G)u^i=\prod_{j=2}^r(1+x_ju)$. Substitute into Step 7 and use $x=x_1$ to obtain the required product for $F$. Taking the coefficient of $u^r$ gives $c_r(F)=x_1\cdots x_r$. This closes the induction for every $r$. The coordinate nonzerodivisor argument was over an arbitrary ring; no step assumed S reduced, regular or smooth, and the filtration was split only on local charts.

Checked nonsplit filtrations, singular bases and ranks zero and one. Recorded Stacks proof typos in report.md; the item statement is unchanged. lean.statement: theorem chern_flag_formula (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) {S : Scheme.{u}} (a : S ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) [IsSeparated a] [LocallyOfFiniteType a] [QuasiCompact a] (F : S.Modules) (r : ℕ) [F.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank r] (H : Fin (r + 1) → S.Modules) (ι : ∀ i : Fin (r + 1), H i ⟶ F) (d : ∀ j : Fin r, H j.castSucc ⟶ H j.succ) (hmono : ∀ i : Fin (r + 1), Mono (ι i)) (hcompat : ∀ j : Fin r, d j ≫ ι j.succ = ι j.castSucc) (hzero : IsZero (H 0)) (hfull : IsIso (ι (Fin.last r))) (hsub : ∀ i : Fin (r + 1), (cokernel (ι i)).IsLocallyFree) (hQ : ∀ j : Fin r, (cokernel (d j)).IsInvertible) : (∀ i : Fin (r + 1), P.ordinaryFiniteChernClass a F r i.val = P.ordinaryFiniteFlagProductCoefficient S r (fun j => P.ordinaryFiniteFlagRoot a (cokernel (d j)) (hQ j)) i.val) ∧ P.ordinaryFiniteChernClass a F r r = P.ordinaryFiniteFlagTopProduct S r (fun j => P.ordinaryFiniteFlagRoot a (cokernel (d j)) (hQ j))
